title: Affine free presentations for finite-type constructible modules over Noetherian rings
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $R$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Work with sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaf $R_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. A sheaf of $R_X$-modules is called constructible if it admits a finite partition by locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] whose strata are constructible subsets of $X$ [def-weil-constructible-subset] and on which its inverse-image restrictions are locally constant with finitely generated $R$-module values [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Every constructible sheaf $F$ admits finite families of affine etale $X$-schemes $U_i$ and $V_j$ and an exact sequence $\bigoplus_{j=1}^m j_{V_j!}R_{V_j}\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{i=1}^n j_{U_i!}R_{U_i}\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow0$, where $j_!$ is the sheafified etale sum-extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. Both $m,n$ may be zero. There is no finiteness requirement on the underlying sets of $R$ or of the module values. The constructibility of the strata is part of the hypothesis; it is automatic when $X$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 095N, lemma-category-constructible-modules, statement and proof, etale-cohomology.tex lines 12412-12466.

proof.text: First relate global and affine-local constructibility for this qcqs X. Over Noetherian R every finitely generated value M is finitely presented: apply the cited submodule theorem with F=M and G=M. A global stratification restricts to affine opens by base change. Conversely choose a finite affine open cover and local constructibility stratifications. The cited gluing theorem gives a global finite constructible immersed refinement, with actual morphisms from each resulting stratum to a local stratum. Pull back the local constant charts along these morphisms; pullback of constant sheaves is constant. Thus the affine-local predicate in the Noetherian Serre theorem agrees with the global predicate used here. Consequently its zero, kernel, cokernel and extension conclusions hold in our convention. In particular finite sums are constructible: induct using the split exact sequence from a partial sum to that sum plus one term, with quotient the last term.

source.place: Tag 03RZ(3); Tag 095E (lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), affine-local to global passage

proof.text: Write P(W) for the sheafification of the free R-module presheaf V mapping to the finite-support R-linear combinations of Hom_X(V,W). It identifies with j_W! R_W: sending a basis symbol s to the constant section 1 in the s-indexed summand gives a map from the free presheaf to the sum-extension presheaf. Locally each coefficient section of R_V is a constant coefficient; hence a finite sum of such sections is locally in this map, and a vanishing combination of constant coefficients is locally already zero. The local injectivity and surjectivity criterion for abelian sheafification makes the induced map an isomorphism; it is R-linear, and its inverse is linear by composing the scalar-action equality with that isomorphism. After sheafification the inverse identities hold, since both send each summand generator to itself and every local section is locally such a finite combination. The restrictions in both formulas compose the same indices.

source.place: Modules on Sites Tag 03DI, explicit sum-extension and module sheafification

proof.text: For each affine etale W to X, use the qcqs etale stratification theorem to choose a finite constructible locally closed stratification i_a:X_a to X with W_a=W times_X X_a finite etale over X_a. The module base-change isomorphism and pullback of constants identify i_a^{-1}j_W! R_W with pi_a! R_Wa. The finite-etale shriek-star isomorphism identifies this with pi_a* R_Wa. The cited finite-etale pushforward theorem makes this locally constant with finitely generated R-module values: R_Wa is constant of finite type, with value the cyclic R-module R. Thus these particular constructible strata witness constructibility of P(W) by the preceding identification. This writes out the source proof of 03S8(3) and retains the constructibility of the strata, which the older sum-extension node did not explicitly include in its statement.

We prove the finite affine epimorphism construction for an arbitrary constructible G, so it can later be applied to a kernel. Use a small skeleton of the affine etale objects and let I consist of pairs (W,f) with f:P(W) to G. For finite S contained in I, let E_S be the finite sum of its P(W) and q_S:E_S to G the map with components f. Steps 1-3 make E_S and C_S=coker(q_S) constructible. The cited support statement makes T_S=Supp(C_S) constructible and says that vanishing at one geometric point over x excludes x from this support. Exactness of abelian geometric stalks identifies (C_S)_x with coker((q_S)_x): module cokernels have the same underlying sheafified abelian cokernels. Thus x lies outside T_S exactly when the finite family is surjective on that stalk.

For every x, the stalk G_x is finitely generated: lift the geometric point to a member of a trivializing etale covering using the cited covering-point lifting theorem and restrict the given stratum chart through x and identify its stalk with its finitely generated constant value. The cited inverse-image stalk comparison and constant-sheaf stalk theorem justify these identifications. Apply affine free finite-stalk generation to get some finite S with (q_S)_x surjective. Step 4 then gives x outside T_S. Therefore the intersection of all T_S over finite S is empty.

source.place: Tag 095N, sentence using finite type of each stalk

proof.text: The underlying space of X is spectral by the qcqs-spectral theorem. Apply the constructible finite-intersection theorem to the sets T_S: finitely many T_S1,...,T_Sr have empty intersection. Put S equal to the union of these finitely many finite subsets. Every q_Sa factors through q_S, so surjectivity for any q_Sa implies surjectivity for q_S. Thus T_S is contained in their intersection and is empty. If the selected family is empty then X is empty and take S empty. By exact stalks every stalk of C_S is zero; stalk conservativity applied to the underlying abelian map C_S to zero makes C_S zero. Its module object is then zero too, since a zero underlying sheaf admits only the zero scalar action. Hence q_S is an epimorphism. This finishes the finite affine epimorphism construction for every constructible G.

Apply Steps 4-6 to G=F to obtain q:E_0 to F with E_0 a finite affine free sum and q epi. Step 1 makes K=ker(q) constructible because E_0 and F are constructible. Apply the same Steps 4-6 with G=K; this is a second application of the proved construction, not an induction assumption. It gives an epimorphism p:E_1 to K with E_1 another finite affine free sum. For the inclusion i:K to E_0, set a=i composed with p. Since p is epi, image(a)=K=ker(q), so the sequence E_1 to E_0 to F to zero is exact. Equivalently any map h:E_0 to H with h a=0 satisfies h i=0 by epimorphy of p, and factors uniquely through q; this is the cokernel universal property. Reindex the two finite sets as 1,...,m and 1,...,n and use Step 2 to write each summand as j_!R. Empty sets, zero F, empty X and the zero ring are all permitted.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-5fd2ec7a4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 23 cited statements; there are no new nodes and no fixes. The item gives the forward direction of Stacks 095N (etale-cohomology.tex 12412-12466) with the same hypotheses: qcqs X, Noetherian R, constructible locally closed strata, finitely generated (f.g.) values, and no finite-set requirement. The statement change is only the backslash normalisation, so the target is not weakened. Steps: (1) Noetherian f.g. ⇒ f.p., and the local-gluing core node makes the global and affine-local predicates agree, so the Noetherian Serre closure applies; tracing a constructible set on an affine (retrocompact) open is two lines. (2) Sheafification of the free presheaf ≅ j_!R_W: checked against the sum-extension blueprint_update, local injectivity and surjectivity both hold. (3) 03S0, 03S6, 03S7 and finite-étale pushforward apply because W is affine and therefore qcqs, and the strata are constructible; this rewrites the argument of lem-per-noetherian-etale-sum-constructible rather than citing that weaker statement. (4) The support node's explicit statement defines constructible inline with f.g. values, consistent with its landed Lean IsConstructibleSheaf, and its proof does not use finite sets. (5) Point lift, stalk comparison and f.g. stalk generation. (6) Spectral compactness: the containment for the union of the finite subfamily is correct, the empty-family case gives X=∅, and conservativity finishes. (7) Second application to the kernel, elementary. Edge cases checked: X=∅, F=0, R=0, R=ℤ, infinite R. No cycle (closure of 912 nodes). new-constructible-affine-free-presentation-general is an overlap only under the finite-stalk def-constructible-constructible; noted for the maintainer, not cited. Batch-5: lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented is a pure-algebra Mathlib leaf with empty proof_deps, outside both assumptions, so it is accepted. All 19 declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. No SGA is cited.

lean.statement: theorem exists_noetherian_affine_free_presentation (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (R : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R)) [IsConstructibleSheaf F] : ∃ (n m : ℕ) (U : Fin n → X.Etale) (V : Fin m → X.Etale), (∀ i : Fin n, IsAffine (U i).left) ∧ (∀ j : Fin m, IsAffine (V j).left) ∧ ∃ (f : finiteAffineFreeCoproduct X R m V ⟶ finiteAffineFreeCoproduct X R n U) (g : finiteAffineFreeCoproduct X R n U ⟶ F) (w : f ≫ g = 0), Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ g w))
lean.note: The two real-data helper definitions specialize the recorded etale sum-extension and finite categorical coproduct; no new constructibility predicate is introduced. IsConstructibleSheaf uses constructible immersed strata and finitely generated module stalks, with no finite-set hypothesis.
